domain: Prior art — open-source iOS quantified-self / life-logging apps, health exporters, location life-loggers, HealthKit wrappers, screen-time exporters, and self-hosted personal-data dashboards (surveyed 2026-07-24 via authenticated GitHub API + App Store lookup API; every repo's activity status is from live `pushed_at`, not memory)

capabilities.framework: Home Assistant iOS companion (Apache-2.0, 2,271★, pushed 2026-07-24 — the single most battle-tested answer to "what can an iOS app report")
capabilities.backfill: none as shipped — HA queries only the last 10 minutes (`Current.calendar().date(byAdding:.minute,value:-10)`), but CMMotionActivityManager itself backfills ~7 days
capabilities.resolution: latest sample in a 10-min window; State = activityTypes.first, Attributes = {Confidence, Types[]}
capabilities.notes: Worth stealing: HA emits the FULL activityTypes array as an attribute, not just the top type — CMMotionActivity can assert several simultaneously. Collapsing to one loses data.

capabilities.backfill: CMPedometer backfills ~7 days; HA queries startOfDay→now on every update
capabilities.notes: The 7 pedometer_* IDs are NOT members of the WebhookSensorId enum — they live in a private nested `enum PedometerSensor: String`. Reading the enum alone undercounts HA's sensor surface by 9 (7 pedometer + 2 battery).
Optional keypath — nil on devices without distance estimation.
Requires barometer hardware (CMPedometer.isFloorCountingAvailable).
nil while stationary — LocoKit2 explicitly stores nil-as-zero for this reason (`// store nil as zero, because CMPedometer returns nil while stationary`).
ID prefix is `battery.uniqueID ?? "battery"` so multi-battery devices (Mac) fan out. Attributes carry `Low Power Mode`.
Charger connect/disconnect is one of the highest-signal free life-log events — no permission at all.

capabilities.resolution: snapshot; Attributes = Total, Available, Available (Important), Available (Opportunistic)
capabilities.notes: The Important/Opportunistic split comes from URLResourceKey volumeAvailableCapacityForImportantUsage — most devs only report one number and miss that iOS reports three.

capabilities.permission: Location When-In-Use/Always (iOS 13+ gate on SSID) + NEHotspotNetwork
capabilities.entitlement: com.apple.developer.networking.wifi-info — PAID Apple Developer Program only
capabilities.notes: THE entitlement dividing line for project 172: SSID/BSSID need a signed wifi-info entitlement, which a free Apple ID cannot provision. HA falls back to "Not Connected". Proxy on the free tier: NWPathMonitor gives interface type (wifi/cellular) with no entitlement.
BSSID is a better room-level presence key than SSID (distinguishes mesh nodes). OwnTracks publishes the same pair as `SSID`/`BSSID` in its location payload.

capabilities.stream: Connection type (wifi / cellular / wired / unknown) + cellular radio technology
capabilities.resolution: event-driven; Attributes include "Cellular Technology" when cellular
capabilities.notes: Free-tier win: interface type needs NO entitlement. HA maps the full CTRadioAccessTechnology* constant set (GPRS, Edge, CDMA1x, WCDMA, HSDPA, HSUPA, CDMAEVDORev0/A/B, eHRPD, LTE, NR=5G, NRNSA=5G NSA).

capabilities.resolution: snapshot; Attributes = Carrier ID, Carrier Name, MCC, MNC, ISO Country Code, Allows VoIP, Current Radio Technology
capabilities.notes: CONTESTED/STALE: CTCarrier is deprecated since iOS 16 and returns placeholder values (carrierName "--", MCC/MNC "65535") on iOS 16.4+. HA still ships this code; expect it to be dead weight on iOS 26. Do not build on it.

capabilities.resolution: one placemark per location update; 15 attributes
capabilities.notes: Exact attribute set worth copying verbatim: Administrative Area, Areas Of Interest, Country, Inland Water, ISO Country Code, Locality, Location[lat,lon], Name, Ocean, Postal Code, Sub Administrative Area, Sub Locality, Sub Thoroughfare, Thoroughfare, Time Zone, Zones[]. CLGeocoder is free/keyless but rate-limited — HA holds a strong ref to the geocoder to survive ARC (`withExtendedLifetime`), a real bug most implementations hit.
Free tier, no entitlement. Only boolean isFocused — the NAME of the active Focus mode is NOT exposed to third-party apps; Shortcuts Focus automations are the only route to which mode.

capabilities.stream: Current audio output route (speaker / headphones / AirPods / CarPlay / …)
capabilities.notes: Zero-permission AirPods-connected signal, and a car-presence signal via CarPlay/Bluetooth-A2DP port types. Joins multiple outputs with ", " — keep them as an array instead.

capabilities.backfill: none for live altimeter (CMSensorRecorder/SensorKit ambientPressure is the archival path)
capabilities.notes: OwnTracks publishes the same value as `p` in its location payload (kPa) under `extendedData`.

capabilities.stream: Paired Apple Watch battery level + state
capabilities.resolution: whatever the watch pushes via WCSession application context
capabilities.notes: Proves the watch can inject arbitrary sensor rows into the phone's payload without an App Group — WCSession is the channel. Relevant to project 172's deferred-extension question.

COPY THIS WHOLESALE for project 172's launch ledger. Exact cases: RegionEnter, RegionExit, GPSRegionEnter, GPSRegionExit, BeaconRegionEnter, BeaconRegionExit, Manual, SignificantLocationUpdate, BackgroundFetch, PushNotification, URLScheme, XCallbackURL, Siri, Visit, AppShortcut, Launch, Periodic, Signaled, Unknown, watchContext. Each carries a measured `oneShotTimeout`: 20 s for region/visit events, 10 s for SLC/background-fetch/push/watch, 30 s for user-initiated. Those numbers are HA's field-earned budget for how long iOS actually lets you run per wakeup type.

capabilities.stream: Location fix + zone membership (the webhook payload)
capabilities.api: WebhookUpdateLocation.swift → keys: gps[lat,lon], gps_accuracy, battery, location_name, in_zones[], speed, altitude, course, vertical_accuracy
capabilities.backfill: none — CLVisit/SLC history is NOT retroactively queryable
capabilities.notes: Sentinel discipline worth stealing: HA only emits speed/course/altitude/vAcc/hAcc when > -1, because CoreLocation returns -1 for "invalid" rather than nil. Naively serialising gives you a database full of -1s.
Self-telemetry: recording your own permission state alongside data lets you explain gaps years later. Project 172 should do this for every permission, not just location.
Stamping the collector version on every row is how you later disambiguate a schema change from a behaviour change. Cheap; do it.

capabilities.stream: Frontmost application bundle ID (macOS/Catalyst ONLY — the sensor iOS does not get)
capabilities.notes: NEGATIVE FINDING, and an important one: the most-mature open-source iOS telemetry client on earth ships per-app foreground tracking ONLY on macOS, via a loaded MacBridge.bundle. There is no iOS equivalent in the codebase. Corroborates that per-app usage on iOS has no sanctioned in-process API.

capabilities.stream: Screen active / idle (macOS-only), display count, primary display name/ID (macOS-only), camera+microphone in-use (macOS-only), kiosk mode/brightness/volume/screensaver (iPad kiosk), camera motion, camera stream
capabilities.api: WebhookSensorId cases: active, displays_count, primary_display_name, primary_display_id, camera, microphone, audio_output, kioskMode, kioskBrightness, kioskVolume, kioskScreensaver, cameraMotion, cameraStream
capabilities.notes: Listed for completeness of the 23-provider registration in Environment.swift, but NOT reachable on iPhone. Registration order (all 23): Activity, Pedometer, Battery, Storage, Connectivity, Geocoder, InputOutputDevice, Display, Active, FrontmostApp, Focus, LastUpdate, WatchBattery, AppVersion, LocationPermission, AudioOutput, Barometer, KioskMode, KioskBrightness, KioskVolume, KioskScreensaver, CameraMotion, CameraStream.

capabilities.stream: Location report — full key set (the battle-tested wire schema)
capabilities.framework: OwnTracks iOS (429★, pushed 2026-07-21; App Store v26.2.3, minOS 17.6; release 26.1.1 notes = "iOS 26 adaptation")
capabilities.api: _type=location — keys: lat, lon, tst, created_at, acc, alt, vac, vel, cog, batt, bs, rad, t, tid, p, poi, image, imagename, conn, tag, topic, inregions[], inrids[], SSID, BSSID, m, motionactivities[]
capabilities.entitlement: none for the payload; com.apple.developer.networking.wifi-info for SSID/BSSID
capabilities.backfill: none — publishes live state only; gaps are permanent (offline messages are queued, not reconstructed)
capabilities.resolution: per fix; `m` distinguishes significant(1) vs move(2) monitoring mode
capabilities.notes: The `t` trigger codes are the most valuable single field and map 1:1 to a CoreLocation strategy: p=random background-task ping, c=circular region enter/leave, C=+follow region, b=beacon region, r=response to reportLocation cmd, u=manual, t=timer in move mode, v=**updated by Settings→Privacy→Location Services→System Services→Frequent Locations monitoring** (i.e. CLVisit). Also note `created_at` vs `tst`: message-construction time vs GPS-fix time — keeping both is how you detect queued/offline replay. `motionactivities[]` piggybacks CMMotionActivity into the location row rather than a separate stream.

capabilities.api: _type=transition — keys: wtst, lat, lon, tst, acc, tid, event(enter|leave), desc, t(c|b|l), rid
capabilities.resolution: one message per crossing; MQTT published non-retained
capabilities.notes: Carries `wtst` = timestamp of WAYPOINT CREATION alongside the event time — lets you reason about which fence version fired years later. Almost nobody does this.

capabilities.api: _type=status → iOS object: altimeterAuthorizationStatus, altimeterIsRelativeAltitudeAvailable, backgroundRefreshStatus, deviceIdentifierForVendor, deviceModel, deviceSystemName, deviceSystemVersion, deviceUserInterfaceIdiom, locale, localeUsesMetricSystem, locationManagerAuthorizationStatus, motionActivityManagerAuthorizationStatus, motionActivityManagerIsActivityAvailable, noMap, noRevgeo, pedometerIsDistanceAvailable, pedometerIsFloorCountingAvailable, pedometerIsStepCountingAvailable, version
capabilities.notes: THIS IS PROJECT 172'S PROBE REPORT, already designed and shipped by someone else. 19 fields, each an availability/authorisation predicate with the exact Apple API it wraps documented inline. Steal the field list verbatim for `probe-report.json`; it costs nothing and is proven.

capabilities.stream: Step count over an arbitrary window
capabilities.notes: Note `from`/`to` are the EFFECTIVE period, which may differ from the requested one — the schema admits that iOS truncates your query. Copy that honesty.

capabilities.api: _type=beacon — keys: desc, uuid, major, minor, tst, acc, rssi, prox(0..3)
capabilities.resolution: continuous while ranging — OwnTracks warns it "publishes a lot of messages and has a strong impact on battery life"
capabilities.notes: prox: 0=unknown, 1=immediate, 2=near, 3=far. Docs even give the RSSI→distance relation: RSSI[dBm] = −(10n·log10(d) − A). Cheap indoor room-level presence if you plant beacons.

capabilities.api: _type ∈ {beacon, card, cmd, configuration, encrypted, location, lwt, request, status, steps, transition, waypoint, waypoints} — iOS supports all 13; Android lacks beacon, request, steps
capabilities.notes: `lwt` = MQTT Last Will and Testament — the broker publishes it when the phone's connection dies, giving you a machine-detectable "collector went dark" marker. Project 172's VM-side ingest should synthesise the same thing (server-side staleness alarm), since HTTP has no LWT.

capabilities.stream: Per-sample locomotion record (the canonical on-device life-log row)
capabilities.framework: LocoKit2 — engine behind Arc Timeline (MPL-2.0, 32★, pushed 2026-07-24 TODAY; predecessor LocoKit LGPL-3.0, 1,542★, pushed 2025-03-25)
capabilities.api: LocomotionSample table: id, lastSaved, rtreeId, date, source, sourceVersion, secondsFromGMT, movingState, recordingState, disabled, timelineItemId, latitude, longitude, altitude, horizontalAccuracy, verticalAccuracy, speed, course, stepHz, xyAcceleration, zAcceleration, heartRate, classifiedActivityType, confirmedActivityType
capabilities.entitlement: HealthKit for the heartRate column; App Groups for the multi-app recorder
capabilities.backfill: none live; ImportManager reconstructs from exports
capabilities.resolution: ~1 sample/second while recording; sleep-mode drops to a 30 s cycle, standby to 120 s
capabilities.notes: Two design choices to copy: (1) `secondsFromGMT` is NULLABLE with the comment "pre-2019 samples have no timezone" — a decade-old life-log will have schema archaeology, plan for nullable provenance; (2) `classifiedActivityType` and `confirmedActivityType` are SEPARATE columns — machine guess and human correction never overwrite each other. Also GRDB + an R*Tree virtual table (SampleRTree) for spatial queries, with the covering index on (date, rtreeId, confirmedActivityType, xyAcceleration, zAcceleration, stepHz).

capabilities.stream: Timeline item (visit or trip) with health rollups
capabilities.api: TimelineItemBase: id, lastSaved, isVisit, startDate, endDate, source, sourceVersion, disabled, deleted, locked, samplesChanged, previousItemId, nextItemId, stepCount, floorsAscended, floorsDescended, averageAltitude, activeEnergyBurned, averageHeartRate, maxHeartRate — plus TimelineItemVisit(latitude, longitude, radiusMean, radiusSD, placeId, confirmedPlace, uncertainPlace, customTitle, streetAddress, locality, countryCode) and TimelineItemTrip(distance, speed, classifiedActivityType, confirmedActivityType, uncertainActivityType)
capabilities.notes: The doubly-linked list (previousItemId/nextItemId with deferred FKs and onDelete .setNull) is what makes edge-healing/merging tractable. HealthKit values are DENORMALISED onto the timeline item — the segment, not the day, is the join key. That is the single best idea in the schema: it turns "heart rate" into "heart rate at Starbucks last Tuesday".

capabilities.stream: Place (visited location with learned occupancy histograms)
capabilities.api: Place table: id, source, rtreeId, isStale, latitude, longitude, radiusMean, radiusSD, secondsFromGMT, name, streetAddress, countryCode, locality, mapboxPlaceId/Category/MakiIcon, googlePlaceId/PrimaryType, foursquarePlaceId/CategoryId/CategoryV2Id, visitCount, visitDays, lastVisitDate, arrivalTimes, leavingTimes, visitDurations, occupancyTimes (BLOB Histograms)
capabilities.entitlement: none (external place IDs are optional API enrichments)
capabilities.resolution: one row per learned place; histograms accumulate over years
capabilities.notes: arrivalTimes/leavingTimes/visitDurations/occupancyTimes stored as compressed Histogram blobs — the app learns "when am I usually here" and uses it to disambiguate future visits. Three competing place providers (Mapbox/Google/Foursquare) modelled side by side rather than one canonical ID: correct, because none of them covers everything.

capabilities.api: DailyRecordingStats: dayKey, utcOffset, secondsRecording, secondsSleeping, secondsWakeup, secondsStandby, restartCount, wakeupCount, wakeupTimeoutCount, chainStallCount, appLaunchCount, samplesRecorded
capabilities.notes: THE most directly stealable thing in this entire survey for project 172's Phase-0 probe. It is a measured answer to "did iOS actually keep my app alive today", broken down by state, with failure counters (wakeupTimeoutCount, chainStallCount) rather than a boolean. Implement this on day one and the launch-ledger question answers itself with data instead of forum posts.

capabilities.api: ActivityType enum: unknown(-1), bogus(0), stationary(1), walking(2), running(3), cycling(4), car(5), airplane(6), train(20), bus(21), motorcycle(22), boat(23), tram(24), tractor(25), tuktuk(26), songthaew(27), scooter(28), metro(29), cableCar(30), funicular(31), chairlift(32), skiLift(33), taxi(34), hotAirBalloon(35), skateboarding(50), inlineSkating(51), snowboarding(52), skiing(53), horseback(54), swimming(55), golf(56), wheelchair(57), rowing(58), kayaking(59), surfing(60), hiking(61)
capabilities.resolution: per-sample classification via CoreML models keyed by geohash (ActivityTypesModel table, with depth + accuracyScore + bounding box)
capabilities.notes: Raw values are deliberately sparse (1-6, 20-35, 50-61) so new types slot into a band without renumbering — good schema hygiene for a decade-long log. The classifier trains PER GEOGRAPHIC REGION (geoKey), because 'car' looks different in Bangkok than Dallas.

capabilities.stream: 213 HealthKit type identifiers — the complete, machine-generated enumeration
capabilities.api: Sources/SpeziHealthKit/Resources/en.lproj/Localizable-HKTypes.strings — 213 entries keyed by exact HKQuantityTypeIdentifier* / HKCategoryTypeIdentifier* / HKCorrelationTypeIdentifier* raw strings, each mapped to Apple's own display name
capabilities.entitlement: com.apple.developer.healthkit (+ .background-delivery) — this is THE tier-1 question for a free Apple ID
capabilities.backfill: years — HealthKit is the only iOS store that genuinely backfills, which is why a signing lapse self-heals here but not for location
capabilities.notes: File header says "THIS FILE IS AUTO-GENERATED! DO NOT EDIT!!!" — Stanford regenerates it against the current SDK, so it tracks iOS 26 without you doing anything. MIT-licensed, drop-in. Do not hand-type a HealthKit type list; take this one and diff it each SDK bump. (Full per-type detail is the HealthKit domain agent's deliverable; this row is the source to build it from.)

capabilities.stream: HealthKit background delivery + anchored incremental sync
capabilities.backfill: anchored — HKQueryAnchor persists the high-water mark across launches
capabilities.notes: SleepSessionsBuilder is the non-obvious win: HealthKit gives you fragmented sleep CATEGORY samples, not sessions; stitching them into nights is a solved problem here. Also ships HealthKit+Linux.swift — server-side type parity so your VM ingest can share the model.

capabilities.framework: SpeziSensorKit (Stanford, MIT, pushed 2026-04-06) — wrapper over Apple SensorKit
capabilities.entitlement: com.apple.developer.sensorkit.reader.allow — REQUIRES APPLE RESEARCH APPROVAL, not self-serve even in the $99 program
capabilities.backfill: data is quarantined 24 h before it is fetchable
capabilities.notes: All 21 SensorKit sensors share the same hard gate. Listing them so the ceiling is documented, not so they get built.
Free-tier substitute: AVCaptureDevice ISO/exposure, or screen brightness as a crude proxy.
Free-tier substitute: CMAltimeter live (HA's BarometerSensor) — live only, no archive.
Free-tier substitute: HKQuantityTypeIdentifierHeartRate — lower cadence but no research gate.
Fully replaceable free of charge by CMPedometer (HA's PedometerSensor).
Free-tier substitute: HKQuantityTypeIdentifierAppleSleepingWristTemperature.
No free-tier equivalent whatsoever. Raw optical sensor data is research-only.
Free-tier substitute: HKElectrocardiogram via HealthKit — user-initiated recordings only, not continuous.
Free-tier substitute: CLVisit via startMonitoringVisits() — this is exactly OwnTracks' `t=v` trigger, and it needs only a usage string.

capabilities.stream: Device usage report — per-CATEGORY app usage, screen wake/unlock counts, notifications
capabilities.resolution: applicationUsageByCategory, notificationUsageByCategory, webUsageByCategory, screenWakes, unlocks, unlockDuration, totalScreenWakes
capabilities.notes: This is the ONLY sanctioned in-process iOS API that returns app-usage durations to your own process — and it is research-gated, so it is out of reach for project 172. Its existence is why the Screen Time question keeps resurfacing.

Free-tier substitute: CMSensorRecorder (accelerometer only, ~3 days, no entitlement) — project 172's MotionProbe should confirm it still functions on iOS 26; it has been quietly unreliable since ~iOS 15 (see blockers).
No free archival equivalent — CMSensorRecorder records accelerometer only.
No free equivalent. Counts only, never content.
Free-tier partial substitute: CallKit CXCallObserver gives live call start/end for the current session (no history, no numbers).

capabilities.stream: Keyboard metrics (typing speed, deletion rate, path-typing, emoji use)
capabilities.notes: No free equivalent at all. This is the closest iOS gets to a sanctioned keystroke telemetry stream — and it is research-only.

capabilities.stream: Media interaction events in messaging apps
Face metrics (facial expression features from Face ID camera)
capabilities.backfill: **7 DAYS quarantine** — the only sensor with a longer hold than 24 h
capabilities.notes: dataQuarantineDuration = .days(7) vs .hours(24) for every other sensor. If you ever get SensorKit approval, your face-metrics pipeline has a one-week latency floor by design.

Completes the 21-sensor enumeration: onWrist, ambientLight, ambientPressure, heartRate, pedometer, wristTemperature, ppg(17.4+), ecg(17.4+), visits, deviceUsage, accelerometer, rotationRate, messagesUsage, phoneUsage, keyboardMetrics, siriSpeechMetrics, telephonySpeechMetrics, mediaEvents, faceMetrics, odometer — that is 20 distinct SRSensor values (siri/telephony speech share the SRSpeechMetrics sample type), listed as 21 entries in SensorKit.allKnownSensors.

capabilities.stream: 150+ health metrics exported as JSON/CSV/GPX from a shipping iOS app — the proof of what is achievable at the $99 tier
capabilities.framework: Health Auto Export (closed-source app; docs repo Lybron/health-auto-export 254★ pushed 2026-01-11; App Store v9.0.13, updated 2026-07-19, minOS 17.0)
capabilities.api: POST body → data{ metrics[], workouts[], stateOfMind[], medications[], symptoms[], cycleTracking[], ecg[], heartRateNotifications[] }; each metric = {name, units, data[{qty, date "yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss Z"}]}
capabilities.entitlement: com.apple.developer.healthkit + background-delivery (background auto-export is its Premium tier — i.e. it needs the paid entitlement)
capabilities.backfill: full HealthKit history, aggregatable seconds → yearly
capabilities.resolution: user-selectable: seconds, minutes, hours, days, weeks, months, years
capabilities.notes: Full metric list at .../wiki/Supported-Data, grouped exactly as: Activity (22), Body Measurements (7), Heart (9), Hearing (2), Nutrition (34), Mindfulness (1), Mobility (7), Reproductive Health (1), Respiratory (4), Sleep (1), Vitals (5), Other (10). Special-cased payload shapes to copy: Blood Pressure {systolic,diastolic}, Heart Rate {Min,Avg,Max}, Sleep aggregated {totalSleep,asleep,core,deep,rem,sleepStart,sleepEnd,inBed,inBedStart,inBedEnd} vs unaggregated {startDate,endDate,qty,value∈(Awake|Asleep|In Bed|Core|REM|Deep|Unspecified)}, Blood Glucose {qty, mealTime}.

capabilities.stream: On-device TCP query server — pull architecture that inverts "the VM can't reach an idle iPhone"
capabilities.framework: Health Auto Export TCP/MCP server (HealthyApps/health-auto-export-mcp-server, MIT, 57★, pushed 2026-05-04)
capabilities.api: TCP listener inside the iOS app; client_example.ts + MCP wrapper; docs/tcp-server.md
capabilities.entitlement: none for the network listener itself
capabilities.notes: Proves an iPhone can act as a queryable data SERVER on the LAN, no cloud. Caveat that matters: it works only while the app is foregrounded/active, which is precisely why HAE also sells background push export. For project 172 the honest read is: pull is a great debugging/ad-hoc channel, push remains the only reliable sync.

capabilities.stream: Legitimate per-app Screen Time export (iPhone + iPad), including app bundle IDs and open/close timestamps
capabilities.framework: ActivityWatch/aw-import-screentime (78★, pushed 2026-06-25) — the ONLY working, currently-maintained solution found
capabilities.api: Reads ~/Library/Biome/streams/restricted/App.InFocus/remote/<device_id>/* (SEGB binary + protobuf, parsed by cclgroupltd/ccl-segb) and ~/Library/Biome/sync/sync.db for device names; `aw-import-screentime watch` streams new focus events into ActivityWatch buckets with per-device watermarks
capabilities.permission: macOS Full Disk Access for the terminal; iCloud "Share Across Devices" enabled on BOTH the iOS device and the Mac
capabilities.entitlement: none — it is not an app, it is a filesystem reader
capabilities.backfill: whatever Biome retains on disk — supports on-demand backfill and raw protobuf inspection
capabilities.resolution: individual app focus events with timestamps, i.e. finer than Apple's own Screen Time UI
capabilities.notes: THIS IS THE ANSWER TO 'has anyone solved per-app screen time legitimately' — YES, and it requires a Mac. The iPhone's own usage telemetry syncs via iCloud into the Mac's Biome store under `/remote/<device_id>/`; the Mac is purely a sync sink. Nothing is jailbroken and no private API is called on the phone. See blockers for why this is unreachable for project 172.

capabilities.stream: Screen Time → Home Assistant / InfluxDB / Grafana pipeline (Mac + iOS)
capabilities.api: collector.py reads macOS knowledgeC.db directly; iOS devices come via aw-import-screentime; exporter.py → screentime.csv → HA sensors + InfluxDB 2.x + Grafana; deduplicating, launchd-scheduled
capabilities.resolution: per app, multi-device with custom names
capabilities.notes: Confirms the same architecture independently and adds the dashboard half. Its explicit dependency on aw-import-screentime for the iOS half is corroborating evidence that no on-phone route exists.

capabilities.stream: Offline forensic parse of App.InFocus (open/close per app per device)
capabilities.api: SEGB v1/v2 + protobuf parser (vendored ccl_segb) over a zipped App.InFocus folder + sync.db; output columns: timestamp, open_close, app_bundle, app_version, last_sync_date, device_identifier, device_name; exports CSV/JSON/Parquet; marimo UI, Dockerfile provided
capabilities.notes: VERIFIED CLAIM CHECK: its README says the folder can be "extracted from an iPhone backup", which would be a Windows-viable route. I grepped every .py in the repo (app.py, parser.py, helper.py, zip_helper.py, ccl_segb/*) for backup|MobileSync|Manifest.db|itunes — ZERO hits. Only the macOS ~/Library/Biome path is implemented. Treat the backup claim as unsubstantiated prose until someone demonstrates it. The output column list is still worth copying as a target schema.

capabilities.stream: Location-history web app / self-hosted Google Timeline replacement — the ingest schema to target
capabilities.framework: Freika/dawarich (AGPL-3.0, 9,870★, pushed 2026-07-23 — by far the largest active project in this space)
capabilities.api: Accepts Overland, OwnTracks, GPX, GeoJSON, Google Maps Timeline, Home Assistant, GPSLogger, PhoneTrack; integrates Immich + Photoprism for geotagged photos; ships its own Dawarich for iOS/Android
capabilities.backfill: bulk import of Google Takeout history
capabilities.notes: Strategic read for project 172: if the phone speaks the OwnTracks or Overland wire format, it gets Dawarich (and Home Assistant, and half a dozen others) for free. Emitting a bespoke schema buys nothing and costs the whole ecosystem. Note AGPL — fine for self-hosting, relevant if code is ever copied.

capabilities.stream: GeoJSON batched location payload (the simplest good wire format)
capabilities.framework: aaronpk/Overland-iOS (Apache-2.0, 715★, pushed 2025-10-23; server: aaronpk/Compass 143★, dontic/wayfinder MIT)
capabilities.api: POST {locations:[{type:"Feature", geometry:{type:"Point",coordinates:[lon,lat]}, properties:{timestamp, altitude, speed, horizontal_accuracy, vertical_accuracy, motion[], pauses, activity, desired_accuracy, deferred, significant_change, locations_in_payload, battery_state, battery_level, device_id, wifi}}], current:{...}, trip:{...}}; server must reply {"result":"ok"}
capabilities.backfill: none — queues locally while offline, flushes in batches (default 200, ~600 B/point)
capabilities.resolution: configurable: up to 1 point/second in Standard mode; SLC-only mode for near-zero battery
capabilities.notes: Two ideas to steal. (1) The explicit ACK contract — the server must return {"result":"ok"} before the phone deletes its local queue; there is even a setting to relax this to any HTTP 2xx, with a warning that doing so can lose data. That is exactly the resumable-projection semantics project 172 wants. (2) Every payload carries the SETTINGS THAT PRODUCED IT (desired_accuracy, pauses, deferred, significant_change) — so a year later you can tell a data gap from a config change.

capabilities.stream: 85-attribute daily-rollup schema — the canonical 'one row per day' target model
capabilities.api: GET /api/2/attributes/templates/ (auth required). Groups→attributes: Activity{steps, steps_active_min, steps_elevation, floors, steps_distance, stand_hours, cycle_min, cycle_distance, active_energy}; Workouts{workouts, workouts_min, workouts_distance}; Productivity{productive_min, neutral_min, distracting_min, commits, tasks_completed, words_written, emails_sent, emails_received, pomodoros_min, keystrokes}; Food and drink{coffees, alcoholic_drinks, energy, water, carbohydrates, fat, fibre, protein, sugar, sodium, cholesterol, caffeine}; Finance{money_spent}; Mood{mood, mood_note, energy_level, stress_level}; Sleep{sleep, time_in_bed, light_sleep, deep_sleep, rem_sleep, sleep_start, sleep_end, sleep_awakenings}; Events{events, events_duration}; Health{weight, body_fat, lean_mass, heartrate, heartrate_max, heartrate_variability, heartrate_resting, meditation_min, menstrual_flow, sexual_activity}; Location{checkins, location}; Media{tracks, articles_read, pages_read, mobile_screen_min, gaming_min, tv_min, movies_min}; Social{facebook_posts, facebook_comments, facebook_reactions, mastodon_posts, mastodon_replies, mastodon_boosts, mastodon_favourites}; Twitter{tweets, twitter_mentions, twitter_username}; Weather{weather_temp_max, weather_temp_min, weather_precipitation, weather_cloud_cover, weather_wind_speed, weather_summary, weather_icon, day_length}
capabilities.resolution: one value per attribute per DAY
capabilities.notes: The value-type discipline is the transferable part: Period = minutes as integer; Time of day = minutes from MIDDAY for sleep_start but minutes from MIDNIGHT for sleep_end (deliberate, so 23:30 and 00:30 bedtimes are adjacent numbers rather than 1410 apart); percentages as 0.0–1.0 floats; mood on a fixed 1–9 integer scale. Note `mobile_screen_min` exists in the schema — Exist gets it from user-side integrations, not from iOS directly.

blockers: PER-APP SCREEN TIME ON THE PHONE — solved, but only on a Mac. The sibling finding in `screentime_findings.md` ('knowledgeC/Biome is full-filesystem-only ⇒ impossible on non-jailbroken device') and my finding (ActivityWatch/aw-import-screentime, 78★, pushed 2026-06-25, reads real iPhone per-app focus events) are BOTH TRUE — they are about different machines. iOS's own App.InFocus telemetry syncs via iCloud 'Share Across Devices' into a Mac's ~/Library/Biome/streams/restricted/App.InFocus/remote/<device_id>/, where a Python tool with Full Disk Access parses SEGB+protobuf and gets timestamped bundle IDs. Nothing jailbroken, no private API on the phone. For project 172 this is unreachable not because Apple forbids it, but because of the project's own no-Mac hard constraint. That converts 'impossible' into 'priced': a Mac mini is the cost of per-app usage data. Worth stating explicitly so the decision is made deliberately rather than by default.

THE IPHONE-BACKUP ROUTE TO SCREEN TIME IS UNPROVEN. ASTER's README claims App.InFocus can be 'extracted from an iPhone backup' — which, if true, would be Windows-viable via iTunes backup and would be the single most valuable finding here. I grepped every Python file in the repo (app.py, parser.py, helper.py, zip_helper.py, ccl_segb/*) for backup|MobileSync|Manifest.db|itunes: zero matches. Only the macOS ~/Library/Biome path is implemented. No prior art I found demonstrates extracting App.InFocus from a Windows-side iTunes backup. Do not architect around it without an empirical test; do consider that test cheap enough to run, since a backup already exists on the machine.

SOMEONE ALREADY TRIED THE OBVIOUS iOS SCREEN-TIME APP AND SHIPPED NOTHING. hoovdc/ScreenTimeExporter (Swift, 4★, 'An iOS app to export Screen Time data to a CSV file') is a Hello-World stub: ContentView.swift is the unmodified Xcode template, and the entitlements file contains an EMPTY com.apple.security.application-groups array. Created 2024-09-30, never developed. If you find this repo later and get excited, don't.

SENSORKIT IS THE ONLY SANCTIONED IN-PROCESS APP-USAGE API AND IT IS RESEARCH-GATED. SRSensor.deviceUsageReport returns per-category app usage, screen wakes, unlocks and notification counts to your own process — no report-extension sandbox, no exfiltration ban. But all 21 SensorKit sensors need com.apple.developer.sensorkit.reader.allow, which Apple grants only for approved research studies; it is not self-serve even inside the $99 Apple Developer Program (unlike Family Controls development, which is). Every SensorKit row in this report documents a ceiling, not a plan.

QS ACCESS IS DEAD. The task named it as a health exporter to evaluate. iTunes lookup on its App Store id 920297614 returns resultCount:0 (delisted), and a name search for 'QS Access' surfaces only competitors (Health Auto Export, Simple Health Export CSV, Heart Reports). It has no public source repository. There is nothing to learn from it that Health Auto Export does not now do better. Related: 'Simple Health Export CSV' (Eric Wolter, v2022.2, last updated 2022-10-03) is effectively abandoned, and its public repo ericwolter/apple-healthkit-csv contains only the marketing landing page, not the app source.

CTCarrier-BASED CARRIER TELEMETRY IS DEPRECATED DEAD WEIGHT. Home Assistant still ships ConnectivitySensor's 'SIM <n>' sensors reading CTCarrier.carrierName / mobileCountryCode / mobileNetworkCode / isoCountryCode / allowsVOIP. Apple deprecated CTCarrier in iOS 16 and it returns placeholder values ('--', '65535') from iOS 16.4 onward. The presence of this code in an actively-maintained 2026 repo is a warning in itself: mature open-source clients carry dead sensors, so verify empirically rather than inferring capability from the existence of a code path. (Radio access technology via CTTelephonyNetworkInfo.serviceCurrentRadioAccessTechnology is the part that still works.)

Wi-Fi SSID/BSSID NEEDS A SIGNED ENTITLEMENT AND THEREFORE FAILS ON A FREE APPLE ID. Home Assistant's connectivity_ssid / connectivity_bssid require com.apple.developer.networking.wifi-info; without it the code path returns 'Not Connected'. This is the clearest free-vs-paid dividing line visible in prior art. The free-tier consolation is that NWPathMonitor interface type (wifi/cellular/wired) and OwnTracks' `conn` field (w/o/m) need nothing at all — you lose network IDENTITY, not network CLASS.

NEITHER HOME ASSISTANT NOR OWNTRACKS BACKFILLS ANYTHING. Both publish live state on a trigger; neither reconstructs history after an outage. OwnTracks queues messages while offline and flushes them, and Overland does the same with an explicit server ACK ({"result":"ok"}) before deleting its local queue — but a period during which the app was not installed or not authorised is simply gone. This corroborates project 172's existing asymmetry note: HealthKit and CMPedometer self-heal, CLVisit and location history do not. No prior art solves this; the only mitigations found are queue-and-ACK durability and recording your own permission/recording state alongside the data (HA's location-permission sensor; LocoKit2's DailyRecordingStats).

CONTESTED — DOES THE VISIBLE BACKGROUND-LOCATION INDICATOR IMPROVE SURVIVAL? Overland's README asserts yes, citing Apple Developer Forums thread 726945: 'With the visible indicator, your app is more likely to continue to receive data in the background.' LocoKit2 takes the opposite operational bet: its default sleep manager sets showsBackgroundLocationIndicator = true, but its newer 'shield regime' (code comment BIG-617) explicitly switches to CLServiceSession(authorization: .always) with showsBackgroundLocationIndicator = false, on the hypothesis that a particular session configuration — not indicator visibility — is what cues Apple's suspensions. Both are field-earned positions from serious developers; neither is an Apple statement. Project 172 should treat indicator visibility as an experimental variable in the probe, not a settled fact. Sources: https://github.com/aaronpk/Overland-iOS (README, 'Show Background Location Indicator') and https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sobri909/LocoKit2/main/Sources/LocoKit2/Managers/LocomotionManager.swift (startRecording / applySleepRegimeConfig).

THE MOST MATURE OPEN-SOURCE iOS TELEMETRY CLIENT REPORTS FRONTMOST APP ONLY ON macOS. Home Assistant's FrontmostAppSensor is implemented via a loaded MacBridge.bundle calling NSWorkspace; there is no iOS code path, and none of its 23 sensor providers reports foreground app on iPhone. Combined with the DeviceActivityReport sandbox and the SensorKit research gate, that is three independent confirmations that iOS exposes no in-process per-app usage to a normal app.

AGPL ON THE BIGGEST DASHBOARD. Freika/dawarich (9,870★) is AGPL-3.0. Fine to self-host and fine to send data to, but copying code from it into project 172 would make project 172 AGPL if ever network-served. Prefer speaking its wire protocol (OwnTracks/Overland format) over lifting its code. Same caution for moonfloof/everything (AGPL-3.0). LocoKit v1 is LGPL-3.0 (LocoKit2 relicensed to MPL-2.0, which is far friendlier); Home Assistant iOS is Apache-2.0; SpeziHealthKit / SpeziSensorKit / hkimport are MIT; Overland is Apache-2.0; OwnTracks iOS is NOASSERTION (unrecognised license file — check before copying code).

NO OPEN-SOURCE iOS APP FOUND THAT DOES WHAT PROJECT 172 WANTS END-TO-END. The closest analogues are all partial: Home Assistant iOS has the widest sensor surface but no local database and no long-horizon store (it fires webhooks and forgets); LocoKit2/Arc has the best on-device store and background survival but is location-and-health only; Health Auto Export has the best health export but is closed-source and paywalls background operation; Overland/OwnTracks are location-only. The niche is real and unoccupied — but that also means there is no reference implementation to fork, only four excellent pieces to assemble. Small recent attempts exist and are worth watching rather than depending on: megabyte0x/healthykit (5★, 2026-07-19, 'privacy-first iOS Apple Health sync for private APIs and self-hosted backends'), aryan12singh/pulsecoach, jinsoowhang/healthkit-exporter.
nonObvious: THE desiredAccuracy = 999 TRICK. LocoKit2 runs TWO CLLocationManagers. The real one keeps distanceFilter = 3 m for high-resolution recording; a second, permanent 'sleepLocationManager' exists only as a keep-alive. In its current 'shield regime' that keep-alive is configured desiredAccuracy = 999 (the code comment says 'just under the magic 1000'), distanceFilter = kCLDistanceFilterNone, showsBackgroundLocationIndicator = false — described in-source as the DTS-prescribed compliant session that 'shields the app so the recording manager can keep its wanted df=3.' The comment's hypothesis is that a sole df=3 session is what cued Apple's background suspensions. A specific, numeric, Apple-DTS-sourced incantation that no documentation states and that a competent developer would never guess. Source: Sources/LocoKit2/Managers/LocomotionManager.swift (applySleepRegimeConfig, BIG-617).

CLServiceSession vs CLBackgroundActivitySession — SAME KEEP-ALIVE, DIFFERENT VISIBILITY COST. LocoKit2 uses CLBackgroundActivitySession() as its long-proven baseline (which FORCES the blue background-location indicator), and CLServiceSession(authorization: .always) in the shield regime (which does NOT force it). If you want 24/7 background location without a permanent status-bar indicator on an app you use yourself all day, that one-line substitution is the difference. Same file, startRecording().

A SLEEP/WAKE CYCLE, NOT CONTINUOUS RECORDING — AND A WATCHDOG BECAUSE THE CYCLE STALLS. LocoKit2's recording states are recording / sleep (30 s cycle) / wakeup (30 s timeout, extended to 60 s while the underground detector is 'warming') / standby (120 s cycle) / off. Because the whole thing is a chain of timers that only fire while the app is alive, it ships a 'chain-liveness watchdog' whose only job is to notice the chain died and restart it. The lesson generalises to any iOS background collector: your scheduler WILL silently stop, and you must instrument for that rather than assume it.

MEASURE YOUR OWN UPTIME AS A FIRST-CLASS TABLE. LocoKit2's DailyRecordingStats — one row per local day: secondsRecording, secondsSleeping, secondsWakeup, secondsStandby, restartCount, wakeupCount, wakeupTimeoutCount, chainStallCount, appLaunchCount, samplesRecorded. Project 172's Phase-0 probe is trying to answer 'does iOS actually keep my app alive'; Arc answers it every day, in production, with counters instead of opinions. Implement this table on day one and the launch-ledger question stops being a research question.

SEPARATE THE MACHINE'S GUESS FROM THE HUMAN'S CORRECTION. LocoKit2 stores classifiedActivityType and confirmedActivityType as two distinct columns on both LocomotionSample and TimelineItemTrip, plus uncertainActivityType / uncertainPlace / confirmedPlace booleans. Overwriting a classifier output with a user edit destroys the training signal AND the provenance. Two columns cost nothing and are unrecoverable if you skip them.

DENORMALISE HEALTH ONTO THE TIMELINE SEGMENT, NOT THE DAY. LocoKit2's TimelineItemBase carries stepCount, floorsAscended, floorsDescended, averageAltitude, activeEnergyBurned, averageHeartRate, maxHeartRate directly on each visit/trip. That single decision is what turns 'my average heart rate in July' into 'my heart rate at the office vs at the gym vs driving' — the join key is the segment. Everyone builds daily rollups; almost nobody builds segment rollups, and the segment is where the insight lives.

COPY HOME ASSISTANT'S 20-CASE TRIGGER TAXONOMY WITH ITS TIMEOUT BUDGETS. LocationUpdateTrigger is not just an enum of labels — each case carries an empirically-chosen oneShotTimeout: 20 s for region/visit wakeups, 10 s for significant-location-change / background-fetch / push / watch-context, 30 s for user-initiated. Those numbers encode years of field observation about how long iOS actually lets you run per wakeup type, and they are the right starting budgets for a sync that must complete before suspension. Source: Sources/Shared/Location/LocationTrigger.swift.

OWNTRACKS ALREADY WROTE PROJECT 172'S PROBE REPORT. Its _type=status iOS object is a 19-field capability/authorisation self-report — altimeterAuthorizationStatus, altimeterIsRelativeAltitudeAvailable, backgroundRefreshStatus, deviceIdentifierForVendor, deviceModel, deviceSystemName, deviceSystemVersion, deviceUserInterfaceIdiom, locale, localeUsesMetricSystem, locationManagerAuthorizationStatus, motionActivityManagerAuthorizationStatus, motionActivityManagerIsActivityAvailable, pedometerIsDistanceAvailable, pedometerIsFloorCountingAvailable, pedometerIsStepCountingAvailable, noMap, noRevgeo, version — and the docs link each field to the exact Apple API it wraps. That is the probe-report schema, already designed, already shipping, already documented. Don't invent one.

OWNTRACKS' `t=v` TRIGGER PROVES SYSTEM 'FREQUENT LOCATIONS' IS REACHABLE FOR FREE. The docs define trigger v as 'updated by Settings/Privacy/Location Services/System Services/Frequent Locations monitoring' — i.e. CLVisit. iOS's own significant-places engine feeds your app via startMonitoringVisits() with nothing but a usage string. SensorKit's SRSensor.visits is the research-gated version of the same idea; the free one has been shipping since iOS 8.

KEEP BOTH TIMESTAMPS: FIX TIME AND SEND TIME. OwnTracks carries `tst` (timestamp of the GPS fix) and `created_at` (when the message was constructed). Without both, an offline queue flushing three hours later is indistinguishable from three hours of real movement. Overland makes the same distinction implicitly via its queue-and-ACK design. This is the cheapest possible insurance against a class of analysis bug that is invisible until it has silently corrupted a year of data.

STAMP EVERY PAYLOAD WITH THE SETTINGS THAT PRODUCED IT. Overland's location properties include desired_accuracy, pauses, deferred, significant_change, activity, and locations_in_payload alongside the actual fix. Years later, that is the only way to distinguish 'I didn't move' from 'I had the app in battery-saving mode'. Project 172 should do the same for every collector: emit the config with the data.

THE EXPLICIT ACK CONTRACT. Overland's server must respond with exactly {"result":"ok"} before the phone deletes its local queue; there is a setting to relax this to any HTTP 2xx, and the README warns it 'may inadvertently lose data if your server has errors.' That is precisely the semantics project 172 wants for 'sync is a derived, resumable projection of the on-device source of truth' — and it is a two-line contract, not a framework.

OVERLAND'S 'RESUME WITH GEOFENCE' FIXES THE pausesLocationUpdatesAutomatically TRAP. iOS's automatic pause saves enormous battery but frequently fails to resume promptly when you start moving (Overland's own testing: pause triggers ~10 min after you stop). Its answer: when updates get paused, register an EXIT geofence at the current location with a user-set radius; leaving it wakes the app and resumes tracking with the previous settings. A geofence used as a wake-up trampoline rather than as a place-of-interest is a technique most implementations never consider.

OVERLAND'S TRIP-SETTINGS OVERLAY. It keeps two complete CoreLocation configurations — a low-frequency ambient one and a high-frequency 'trip' one that is applied when a trip starts and reverted when it ends (including a separate 'prevent screen lock during trip' and a separate indicator setting). Recording resolution as a MODE rather than a constant is how you get detailed tracks when they matter without paying the battery cost all day.

THE MACHINE-GENERATED HEALTHKIT TYPE TABLE. SpeziHealthKit ships Sources/SpeziHealthKit/Resources/en.lproj/Localizable-HKTypes.strings with 213 exact HK*TypeIdentifier keys mapped to Apple's own display names, headed 'THIS FILE IS AUTO-GENERATED! DO NOT EDIT!!!'. MIT, regenerated against the current SDK, localised into de/en/en_GB/es/es_US/fr. Hand-maintaining a HealthKit type list is a recurring waste; take this and diff it at each SDK bump.

HEALTHKIT GIVES YOU SLEEP FRAGMENTS, NOT NIGHTS. SpeziHealthKit ships SleepSession.swift + SleepSessionsBuilder.swift specifically to stitch HKCategoryTypeIdentifierSleepAnalysis samples into coherent sessions. Health Auto Export independently exposes the same duality in its JSON schema — an aggregated sleep object (totalSleep/asleep/core/deep/rem/sleepStart/sleepEnd/inBed/inBedStart/inBedEnd) and an unaggregated per-fragment form. Two unrelated projects both had to solve this; assume you will too.

EXIST.IO MEASURES sleep_start FROM MIDDAY AND sleep_end FROM MIDNIGHT. Deliberate: it makes an 11:30 pm and a 12:30 am bedtime adjacent integers instead of 1,410 apart, so averages and charts behave. A one-line schema decision that prevents an entire category of circular-statistics bugs, and one you only think of after being bitten.

AN iPHONE CAN BE A QUERYABLE SERVER ON YOUR LAN. Health Auto Export runs a TCP server inside the iOS app; HealthyApps/health-auto-export-mcp-server connects to it and re-exposes it over MCP so an LLM can query live health data. It inverts the usual 'the VM can never reach an idle iPhone' constraint — with the caveat that it only works while the app is active, which is exactly why the same vendor also sells background push export. Useful as a debugging/ad-hoc channel, not as the sync backbone.

SPEAK AN EXISTING WIRE FORMAT AND INHERIT AN ECOSYSTEM. Emitting the OwnTracks or Overland payload gets you Dawarich (9,870★), Home Assistant, Compass, Wayfinder, PureTrack, Icecondor, Open Humans and moonfloof/everything for free — servers, dashboards and importers you never have to write. A bespoke schema buys nothing that a translation layer at the VM couldn't provide, and costs all of that. Both formats are fully documented and stable.

ARC SHIPS A SEPARATE 'RECORDER' APP. The App Store lookup shows Arc Timeline 4 (v1.5.1, 2026-07-16, minOS 26.0) AND Arc Timeline Recorder (a distinct app) from the same developer, and LocoKit2's AppGroup.swift implements the arbitration: apps advertise recordingState into a shared UserDefaults suite, gossip over Darwin notifications (AppGroupTalk), and shouldBeTheRecorder concedes when another process is alive and recording, or claims the role when none is. A small always-alive recorder plus a heavy UI app is a production-proven answer to being killed in background — and it needs only com.apple.security.application-groups, which Apple's capability table lists as available on a FREE developer account. LocoKit2 also provides localDatabaseOnly: true as the single-app fallback if App Groups turns out unprovisionable.

HOLD A STRONG REFERENCE TO CLGeocoder OR YOUR CALLBACK NEVER FIRES. Home Assistant's CLGeocoder.geocode(location:) wraps the completion handler in withExtendedLifetime(strongGeocoder) and nils it only inside the handler. A locally-scoped geocoder gets deallocated before the reverse-geocode returns. Cheap bug, silent failure, and it will look like 'the geocoder is rate-limited'.

CoreLocation RETURNS -1, NOT nil, FOR INVALID FIELDS. Home Assistant guards every one: speed, course, altitude, verticalAccuracy, horizontalAccuracy are only serialised when > -1. OwnTracks documents the same rule ('acc, alt, cog, vac, vel are only added if they are not zero'). Serialise naively and you get a database full of -1s that look like real measurements.

CMPedometer RETURNS nil WHILE STATIONARY. LocoKit2 has the comment '// store nil as zero, because CMPedometer returns nil while stationary'. If you treat nil as missing rather than as zero, every period of sitting still becomes a data gap.

MODEL A DECADE OF SCHEMA ARCHAEOLOGY UP FRONT. LocoKit2's LocomotionSample.secondsFromGMT is nullable with the comment 'pre-2019 samples have no timezone', and every table carries `source` + `sourceVersion` columns. A life-log outlives its own schema; provenance columns are how you keep old rows interpretable instead of quietly wrong.

YOU CAN TEST THE WHOLE PIPELINE BEFORE COLLECTING A SINGLE REAL DAY. ashtom/hkimport (MIT, 51★, 2026-05-13) injects HealthKit data into the Simulator or a test device; aminbenarieb/healthkit-data-generator (77★) generates realistic synthetic HealthKit history from natural-language prompts; StanfordBDHG/XCTHealthKit drives the Health app from XCTest. Project 172's VM ingest, schema and dashboard can all be validated on synthetic multi-year history while the phone-side probe is still in flight — the two tracks stop being serial.

THE MAINTAINED INDEX OF THIS ENTIRE SPACE IS woop/awesome-quantified-self (2,744★, pushed 2026-07-06). Check it before concluding something doesn't exist; it is actively curated and covers devices, services and apps well outside GitHub's search reach.
